title: Co-ordinate Geometry
prerequisites: Ability to plot points on a number line.
Understanding of positive and negative directions.
Familiarity with the terms horizontal and vertical.
Basic knowledge of the Pythagoras theorem.

topics.title: The Cartesian Plane and Plotting Points
topics.quick_summary: Two perpendicular number lines divide the plane into four quadrants, and every point is located by an ordered pair (x, y) giving its distances from the two axes.
topics.real_life: A map reference, a seat number in a cinema and a pixel address on a screen are all Cartesian coordinates under different names.

detailed.definition: The x-axis and y-axis intersect at right angles at the origin O(0, 0). The abscissa is the x-coordinate (perpendicular distance from the y-axis) and the ordinate is the y-coordinate (perpendicular distance from the x-axis).
detailed.key_idea: The order matters absolutely: (3, 5) and (5, 3) are different points. This is why (x, y) is called an ordered pair.
detailed.working_principle: Signs of the coordinates identify the quadrant. Points on the x-axis have y = 0, and points on the y-axis have x = 0 — which is how axis membership is tested.
applications: Quadrant I (+,+), II (−,+), III (−,−), IV (+,−), counted anticlockwise.
Graphs of linear equations are drawn by plotting and joining points.
Computer graphics addresses every pixel by a coordinate pair.

points: The origin is (0, 0); the axes divide the plane into four quadrants.
Quadrant signs: I (+,+), II (−,+), III (−,−), IV (+,−).
A point on the x-axis is (a, 0); a point on the y-axis is (0, b).
(x, y) is an ordered pair — reversing it gives a different point.
mistakes: Numbering the quadrants clockwise instead of anticlockwise.
Saying a point on the x-axis has x = 0; it is y that is zero.
topics.memory_hook: 'x first, then y — walk before you climb.'
topics.advanced: Descartes' insight in uniting algebra and geometry meant every geometric statement could become an equation. Coordinate geometry is the bridge that makes calculus, physics and computer graphics possible.

formulas.name: Distance Formula
formulas.variables: (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) = the two points, d = distance between them.
formulas.when_to_use: To find the length of a segment, or to test whether a triangle is isosceles or right-angled.
formulas.common_mistakes: Forgetting to square the differences, or subtracting the coordinates in a mixed order.
formulas.shortcut: Distance from the origin to (x, y) is simply √(x² + y²).
